markdown_report:
At 10% progress, retain **joint lexical-residual HSTU** as the first controlled experiment. The supplied history reports scores of 0.5675 for this direction and 0.5325 for the cold start; these observations do not isolate which changes caused the difference.

Three starting insights guide the experiment. First, shared item representations can transfer interaction supervision across related wording. This targets broad thematic matches that miss specific functions or experiences. Second, candidate and history embeddings must share the lexical module. This lets recent narrow interests influence ranking through the existing causal HSTU. Third, Electronics and Industrial have sampled wrong-rank rates of 10.38% and 8.22%. These identify discrimination targets, while alignment scores near 0.5 provide no evidence of collapse.

Three literature insights define alternatives. HSTU supplies the required backbone [1]. Its released sampled-softmax configuration motivates an objective experiment [2]. ST2SI emphasizes behavioral grounding of text representations [3]. This supports learning lexical usefulness from interactions rather than equating wording with compatibility. HSTU temporal ablations motivate elapsed-time conditioning [4]. They do not establish that stronger recency will improve these Amazon datasets.

The framework separates three intervention axes: **representation** shares item evidence, **objective** improves candidate separation, and **time** conditions historical relevance. Change one axis per experiment.

Scores below use O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Atomic idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lexical residual [1,3] | 3: +controlled adaptation; −established fusion | 7: +sparse-item sharing; −weak scratch semantics | 8: +specificity/recent interests; −needs unobserved | 7: +pair discrimination; −cause unproven | 5: +localized module; −predictor integration |
| 32-negative sampled softmax [2] | 2: +family precedent; −standard objective | 7: +ranking pressure; −budget cost | 5: +fewer weak matches; −no explicit specificity | 8: +targets wrong ranks; −training evidence only | 4: +unchanged inference; −sampling care |
| Learned elapsed-time buckets [1,4] | 3: +task adaptation; −native mechanism | 7: +temporal relevance; −timestamp noise | 7: +current opportunities; −satisfied needs unknown | 5: +tests temporal hypothesis; −diagnostics lack time channel | 6: +single backbone; −timestamp plumbing |

Select the lexical residual because it explicitly targets **broad functional/experiential mismatches** and **weak connection to recent narrow interests**, while addressing Electronics/Industrial ranking errors. Encode titles and descriptions with scratch token embeddings, pool fields separately, project, norm-match, and add a small learned residual to item identity. Share this representation across histories and candidates; preserve the baseline loss.

Keep one checkpoint per category, all four routes, fixed seeds/splits, and training caps. Preserve final-nonpadding readout, diagnostic interfaces, and matching predictor serialization. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Track effective-embedding margins and the twenty-user qualitative assessment; sampled HR cannot establish compatibility or reduced unnecessary purchases. References correspond to the supplied sources below.

idea.description: Replace only the corrected HSTU item-embedding module with a jointly trained identity-plus-lexical residual. Use one shared effective item representation for history inputs and candidate scoring, with exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category. Preserve the baseline objective for this first experiment.
idea.motivation: The selected idea targets two explicit user-facing failures: broadly related recommendations that miss specific functions or experiences, and recommendations weakly connected to recent narrow interests. Scratch title/description features may share useful distinctions across sparse item identities, while the unchanged causal HSTU determines their sequential relevance. The quantitative target is the 10.38% Electronics and 8.22% Industrial sampled wrong-rank rates. Neither those diagnostics nor the supplied trial scores establish that missing lexical information caused the errors. Satisfied needs, physical compatibility, and present intent remain only partially observable.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected HSTU construction, causal masking, objective, optimizer, sampler, checkpoint-selection schedule, and empty-history behavior. Set DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl routing. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, and artifacts beneath the current trial directory. Do not inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

Use only public titles/descriptions and training interactions. Build deterministic category-local vocabularies from text permitted by the baseline catalog protocol, without held-out interaction labels or frequencies. Apply Unicode NFKC normalization and case folding; retain alphanumeric model identifiers and internal identifier punctuation. Reserve PAD=0 and UNK=1, cap vocabulary at 10,000, and order tokens by corpus count with lexical tie-breaking. Truncate titles to 16 tokens and descriptions to 64. Record missingness, truncation, and OOV rates. Do not use reviews, ratings, structured categories, prices, stores, external datasets, or pretrained weights.

Initialize the complete corrected baseline first. Construct new parameters inside an isolated torch.random.fork_rng context, preserving subsequent baseline RNG states and avoiding recursive reinitialization of existing modules. Use shared 32-dimensional scratch token embeddings, separate masked field means, and one bias-free projection to the original item dimension. Initialize token weights with standard deviation 0.02 and projection with Xavier uniform. Keep token padding zero. Do not zero-initialize the projection.

For item i, compute z_i = e_i + sigmoid(a) * stop_gradient(||e_i||) * p_i/max(||p_i||, 1e-3), with sigmoid(a) initially 0.05. Compute pooling, projection, normalization, and addition in FP32. Missing text and item padding receive exactly zero lexical contribution. Preserve baseline gradient clipping if configured and monitor nonfinite gradients. Add new parameters to the corresponding baseline optimizer groups; introduce no separate text optimizer or auxiliary loss.

The effective embedding must implement item_emb(ids) and required embedding metadata. Audit every input and candidate-scoring path so none bypasses the wrapper through the raw identity table. Preserve log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and ModelView broadcasting conventions. Diagnose effective embeddings in chunks; do not report raw identity embeddings as the combined representation. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), including measured metrics and accurate definitions. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module; loader tensors remain B x L. Missing category attributes must remain unavailable, not inferred.

For left-padded histories, read features at the greatest absolute nonpadding index, never count-1. Preserve the baseline policy for empty rows. Save vocabulary, token buffers, architecture configuration, lexical parameters, identity parameters, and backbone together. Update the embedded predictor writer to reconstruct the same architecture, load strictly, call eval(), and load exactly one checkpoint per category. Begin without an effective-table cache. Verify checkpoint/predictor score agreement, causal masking, and zero padding contribution.

Selection uses only the unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10 protocol. Report category results and paired user hit differences when exposed by the host; do not replace host evaluation with training-prefix diagnostics. Track the same measured pair-ranking diagnostics and native full-catalog assessment for five training users per category. Treat qualitative improvement, semantic attribution, and full-catalog relevance as separate questions. Optional title-only or text-shuffling controls require fresh independent training within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget and never combine predictions. The exact supplied baseline source is absent from this prompt, so the pseudocode specifies integration points rather than inventing a runnable replacement train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_REQUIRED_CATEGORIES:
    model = construct_supplied_corrected_hstu_in_original_order()
    assets = deterministic_title_description_tokens(category)
    with isolated_new_parameter_rng(seed=42):
        model.item_emb = LexicalResidual(model.item_emb, assets)

    # LexicalResidual.forward(ids), shared by histories and candidates:
    # e = identity(ids)
    # title = masked_mean(token_embedding(title_tokens[ids]))
    # desc = masked_mean(token_embedding(description_tokens[ids]))
    # p = bias_free_projection(concat(title, desc))
    # r = sigmoid(scale_logit) * detach(norm(e)) * p / clamp(norm(p), min=1e-3)
    # r = where(has_text[ids] AND ids != 0, r, 0)
    # return where(ids != 0, e + r, 0)
    # Compute residual arithmetic in FP32; initial sigmoid(scale_logit)=0.05.

    optimizer = baseline_optimizer_including_new_parameters(model)
    for epoch in range(configured_epochs_at_most_200):
        for step in range(200):
            sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch()
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            pos_score = model.predict_score(features, positive)
            neg_score = model.predict_score(features, negative)
            loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(pos_score, neg_score, positive != 0)
            unchanged_baseline_optimizer_step(loss)
        follow_supplied_validation_and_checkpoint_selection()

    save_one_selected_checkpoint_with_configuration_and_token_assets()

emit_predictor_with_identical_model_classes_and_four_category_routing()

originality.positive: A tightly controlled adaptation combines scratch field pooling, conservative scale matching, and shared HSTU item representations under the diagnostic and single-model contracts.
originality.negative: Identity/text fusion and residual scaling are established techniques; this is an experimental adaptation rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Interaction-grounded lexical sharing could improve sparse-item discrimination and motivate later controlled studies of functional and experiential representations.
future_potential.negative: Mean pooling, sparse supervision, and incomplete metadata may yield lexical shortcuts; gains would not establish compatibility or satisfaction awareness.

code_difficulty.positive: The architectural modification is localized to one shared embedding module and leaves the HSTU backbone and objective intact.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct integration still requires RNG isolation, effective-embedding diagnostics, serialized token assets, and identical training and generated-predictor scoring paths.

related_work.title: HSTU: Actions Speak Louder than Words
contributions: Provides the sequential transducer backbone that this experiment must preserve.
Motivates position and elapsed-time conditioning as a separate architectural direction.
limitations: Does not establish gains from the proposed scratch lexical residual on the four Amazon categories.

related_work.title: Official HSTU sampled-softmax configuration
contributions: The supplied search result identifies a 128-negative sampled-softmax configuration with normalized embeddings and temperature 0.05.
Provides a concrete precedent for a subsequent objective-only HSTU experiment.
limitations: Configuration choices are starting points, not evidence of optimality for this benchmark.
Changing loss, normalization, and temperature together would complicate attribution.

related_work.title: ST2SI
contributions: The supplied summary emphasizes item transitions and text–ID alignment.
Supports grounding textual representations in behavioral supervision.
limitations: Does not validate the specific scratch mean-pooled HSTU implementation.
Textual alignment cannot establish physical compatibility or current user need.

related_work.title: Scaling New Frontiers
contributions: The supplied summary reports controlled position/time attention-bias ablations on MovieLens-20M.
Motivates a separate learned elapsed-time-bucket experiment.
limitations: Results concern another dataset and do not demonstrate transfer to the four Amazon categories.
Temporal gains do not establish persistent/transient intent separation.
